title: Book Two · Chapter 120: A Bowl for Three
story:
By the end of that month, Jun's tree book is dry. The damaged corners are still stiff. When Ronan enters a room, pupils talk about games and lessons again. They do not always mention the guides.

But he still notices when someone looks at the guide box.

On Sunday, Mum asks him to buy noodles with her. Dad is finishing a morning job at Mr Sun's. They plan to meet him near the shop.

At the food stall, the bowls are larger than Ronan expects.

“Three?” the seller asks.

Mum looks at the noodles, then at Ronan.

“Two bowls and one empty bowl, please.”

“I can eat a whole one,” Ronan says.

“Good. You can begin with your share and ask for more.”

Dad arrives with clean hands and a tired face. He sits on the low stool. His knees nearly touch the table.

Ronan pushes the empty bowl toward him.

“A special small meal.”

Dad looks inside. “Very light.”

Mum divides the noodles. Dad holds the bowls steady. They pass pieces of green vegetable from one bowl to another until each person has some.

A long noodle hangs from Ronan's chopsticks. He tries to lift it higher. It keeps rising from the bowl.

“You have caught the whole street,” Dad says.

Ronan laughs and drops it. A little soup lands on the table.

Mum passes him a cloth. He wipes it before it reaches her skirt.

For a while they eat quietly. Nobody asks about school or work. A bicycle bell sounds at the corner. A little child in the next seat asks for more soup. The seller fills the bowl slowly.

Dad finishes first. He leans back and closes his eyes.

“Are you asleep?” Ronan asks.

“Only my face.”

“Your face is smiling.”

“It likes the soup.”

Mum takes the last green leaf from her bowl.

“I am having tea with my friend next week,” she says. “You two can manage supper again.”

Dad opens one eye. “We have a good leaf cook.”

Ronan points at Dad's shoe. There is no leaf on it today.

They leave the stall together. Mum pays from the meal money. Ronan keeps his own few coins in his pocket. This meal is not another bill for his mistake.

At the narrow crossing, Dad holds the empty food packet while Mum ties her shoe. Ronan waits beside them. Then Mum takes his hand. The afternoon is still theirs to enjoy.

They take the long way home, past the square. The sun is warm, and Dad's face is awake again.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

divide＝分配；share＝份额；chopsticks＝筷子；manage＝料理。

## 理解问题

1. 一家人怎样分两大碗面？
2. 这顿饭中有哪些普通快乐？

## 读句子

**Mum / passes him / a cloth.** Mum／递给他／一块布。
